## Claim amendment · domain:ui#4 · 2026-10-27T20:31Z

Thread-read: 6452823300

The card thread (`claude/project-thread-bol9ec`) measured the break. The console registers two `api` handlers, and neither reads `opensInNewTab` / `newTabUrl`; both always fetch the target. The list pages run the one in `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx`, already in the surface. The record header and the ⋯ more-menu run `RecordDetailView.tsx`'s own `apiHandler`, passed in its `ActionProvider` handlers map, which was outside the surface. The fix exports the fast path's own condition from `consoleServerAction.ts`. Both handlers then route an api action that meets it to the existing console server-action handler, which already resolves the record id, pre-opens the tab and substitutes `{recordId}`. No second interpolator.

File surface: `ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/consoleServerAction.ts` (the exported predicate), `ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx`, `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx` (its `apiHandler` only), tests beside (including `RecordDetailView.apiNewTabUrl-26747.test.tsx`), one root changeset; ⛔ `ui/packages/core/**`, `packages/spec/**`, server packages, any new key (stop on breach)
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

An absolute `newTabUrl` (QA's value) is a separate open question. The spec calls the key a path template, and the fast path prefixes `baseUrl`. That behaviour is not changed here.
